answer.justification: The lesser sac lies posterior to the stomach. Laparoscopic access requires opening the lesser omentum (gastrohepatic ligament), which forms the anterior boundary of the lesser sac. The phrenoesophageal ligament fixes the esophagus at the hiatus; the phrenicocolic ligament supports the splenic flexure; the ligamentum venosum is a fetal remnant within the lesser omentum and is not incised for this access.
